source.publication: TIR 95-9: Income Taxation of Contributory Public Employee Pensions of Other States (Massachusetts DOR, 01/10/1996)
source.section: Department's Position After Pariser, Example 2 (age 55, 25,000 New York State contributory pension, no deduction); 2025 Form 1 Instructions PDF p10 Line 4 second bullet and PDF p22-23 Schedule Y Line 13; Form 1 lines 2a, 2c, 4, 15-22

worked: Federal AGI = New York State contributory public employee pension 25,000.00 (person 0) + private pension 15,000.00 (person 0) = 40,000.00 (given). Federal taxable income = 40,000.00 - 15,750.00 standard deduction (15,750.00) = 24,250.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Massachusetts Form 1 (the projection starts from federal AGI and takes out the exempt items): Line 4 taxable pensions = 25,000.00 New York State contributory public employee pension (included in line 4, then Schedule Y line 13) + 15,000.00 private pension (taxed: most private pensions are taxable, PDF p10) = 40,000.00. Line 10 total 5.0% income = 40,000.00. Schedule Y line 13 (New York State contributory pension, TIR 95-9: up to 20,000 a person who has attained 59 1/2): person 0: age 55, not 59 1/2 or older, so no deduction for any of it (TIR 95-9 Example 2) = 0.00; total 0.00 -> Schedule Y line 19 -> Form 1 line 15 = 0.00. Line 16 total deductions = 0.00. Line 17 = 40,000.00 - 0.00 = 40,000.00. Line 2a personal exemption (single) = 4,400.00; line 2c age 65 or over before 2026: 0 x 700.00 = 0.00; line 2g = line 18 = 4,400.00. Line 19 = 40,000.00 - 4,400.00 = 35,600.00. Line 20 interest and dividends = 0.00. Line 21 = 35,600.00. Line 22 = 35,600.00 x 0.05 = 1,780.00. No 8.5%/12% income or long-term gains (lines 23-24 = 0.00); 4% surtax 0.00 (line 21 is under 1,083,150). Line 28 total tax = 1,780.00; no credits (No Tax Status and the Limited Income Credit do not apply: Massachusetts AGI 40,000.00 is over their limits). State income tax = 1,780.00.
